tests: every socket-opening git call is classified, and the ref probe carries its bound
only the destroying caller holds the network licence for reconstruction

consumesExternalOutput.program: git, as `git ls-remote --symref <remote> HEAD` against a TCP listener that accepts and never speaks
consumesExternalOutput.provenance: Rule (f) binds because both mutated modules match the spawn grep, and the obligation is met rather than waved at. The two named tests assert over SOURCE TEXT, which is the right altitude for a CLASSIFICATION; the premise underneath both is a claim about another program, that git does not give up on a stalled peer by itself, and that premise is this capture, taken 2026-09-16 on git 2.43.0 at two different waits (5s and 20s, exit 124 both times, empty output both times) so a reader can see the second is not a longer version of a timeout that had already fired. Both named tests read the capture and require both waits to still be recorded before concluding anything. The two members are structurally different and hit different halves of the classification: the first takes the BOUND off the one call a reporting path must never reach unbounded, whose harm is the hang finding F-1 named; the second takes the network LICENCE away from the destroying caller, whose harm is the opposite and quieter, a teardown on a rehydrated clone that can no longer resolve its default branch and refuses work that should proceed. A witness with only the first member would be green on a round that over-corrected F-1 by removing the licence everywhere.
